06 · Agent handoff

Shared component grammar

Build a case-management interface that can support multiple domains while preserving one component language. CORE CASE OBJECT - Identity: case ID, title, owner, status, current stage - Route: fixed visible progression through stages - Working state: current task, open question, next decision - Carried information: inherited values with visible provenance - Evidence: claims linked to artifacts and verification state - Decision journal: append-only decisions with author, date, and rationale - Supersession: current values appear beside preserved earlier assumptions - Stakeholders: role, influence, impact, and ownership - Output artifact: a readable case summary generated from the work - Inspector: related context without leaving the current workspace DOMAIN ADAPTATION - Project management emphasizes deliverables, dependencies, risks, and milestones - Change management emphasizes stakeholder impact, readiness, interventions, and adoption evidence - Consulting emphasizes problem framing, evidence, hypotheses, recommendations, and client decisions DESIGN RULES - Keep the case shell stable across domains - Change vocabulary and module emphasis, not the whole interface - Show provenance directly in inherited values - Never silently overwrite an earlier judgment - Treat Proceed and No-Go as equally legitimate decisions - Make mobile a different composition, not a compressed desktop - Avoid generic dashboard cards unless the card represents a real case object or artifact
